verdict.rationale: LangGraph's Agent Server (documented as the 'LangGraph Platform runtime', titled 'LangSmith Deployment') exposes API endpoints for assistants, threads, runs, crons and store, published as an OpenAPI 3.1 spec. A hosted deployment control plane at api.host.langchain.com, with a versioned Deployments API, supports deploying to a managed runtime. Every deployed Agent Server ships a /docs endpoint, and the documented workflow runs from local dev to production deployment. The community question about deploying beyond `langgraph serve` is only a question, not a contradiction. Missing for 10: step-by-step managed-deployment docs in the pack (the deploy step is only referenced, not detailed), and independent or hands-on corroboration of calling a managed deployment's endpoint.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can deploy an agent to a managed runtime and call it as an API endpoint

citations.quote: docs.langchain.com publishes the Agent Server (LangGraph Platform runtime) OpenAPI 3.1 document, info title "LangSmith Deployment", covering Assistants
every deployed or locally run Agent Server ships a built-in interactive API docs endpoint
The resulting server exposes all API endpoints for runs, threads, assistants, etc., and includes supporting services such as a managed database for checkpointing and storage.
the endpoint groups are version-labelled (Integrations v1, Deployments v2, Listeners v2)
